title: apex-ayl.101 RED ratchet — cache_write_tokens dropped on the responses wire: a cold-home sol session gets a provider-REPORTED cache write (wire control) that the harness never records (usage.json session.cacheCreationTokens hardcoded 0 pre-cut, conversation.rs From<Usage> for TokenUsage). RED today; GREEN after CACHEWRITE-DTO-1 lands + fresh binary.

steps.prompt: In under 150 words, explain the trade-offs between append-only log storage and in-place update storage for a session history file, with one concrete example of each.
One sentence: which of the two storage styles is better for a crash-prone notebook, and why?

ndjson.label: NO TERMINAL ERROR: the turns completed (the red is the usage mapping, not the turn).

wire.label: CONTROL (premise, class model): the provider REPORTS a non-zero input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens on some captured response frame. regex over RAW capture text: the SSE payload is JSON-escaped inside the 'frame' string and compact (no space after the colon), hence the optional backslash before the quote + \\s* before the value class. 0-hit = no write observed this run = probe meaningless = VACUOUS (never a silent pass, never a false red).

artifact.label: RED PIN (pre-cut FAILs): the harness RECORDS the provider-reported cache write into usage.json session.cacheCreationTokens. Pre-CACHEWRITE-DTO-1 the From<Usage> for TokenUsage mapping hardcodes cache_creation_prompt_tokens: 0 (stale comment '0 on backends without a cache-write signal') — the drop is the defect. Post-cut + rebuild: non-zero on a cold-home session with a reported write.
